column1: # English for a Cebuano root drilled in an affix pattern (tunatale-ve4p.4). Hand-written.
# root<TAB>pattern<TAB>the root's English<TAB>the English of each form, in the pattern's order
# A row here is the ONLY way a root gets into an affix drill. The English is NOT derived from the
# root's gloss, because the affix can change the meaning: kita is "see", but magkita is "will meet"
# and makita is "will see"; dala is "bring", but nadala is "got carried". Measured 2026-10-07 on the
# 13 pairs the owner's deck could drill: wording them mechanically from the gloss got 3 wrong.
# Written 2026-10-07 and checked the same day against John U. Wolff, A Dictionary of Cebuano Visayan
# (1972; Project Gutenberg #40074): each root's entry, its verb class and its example sentences.
# NOT checked by a native speaker. Wolff's classes, as used below: [A] takes mu-/mi- (punctual) and
# mag-/nag- (durative); [A2] takes mu-/mi- only; [B1] is stative, ma-/na-; [C] is mutual action, mag-.
#   adtu [A2] go · anhi [A2] come ("Muanhi ka ba ugma? Will you come here tomorrow?") · balik [A2] go,
#   come back · sulud [A2] go in · inum [A] drink · kaun [A2S] eat · tan-aw [A] see, look at ·
#   lakaw = lakat [A] walk, and [A2] go away (milakaw is also "left") · ampu [A] pray ·
#   dala [A] take, bring, carry ("Magdala ba kug rigalu? Shall I bring presents?") · lutu [A] cook ·
#   hulat [A] wait · uban [AC] go with, accompany ("Muuban ku nimu, I'll go with you") ·
#   tulug [B1] go to sleep ("Natulug na ba siya? Is he asleep yet?") · lipay [B1] be happy
#   ("Nalipay ku nga nia ka, I am glad that you're here") · hurut [A] use up; na- = be used up.
#   kita "meet" is [C]: "Magkita ra tag usab, We'll meet again."
# Two corrections the check made:
# - sulti: "tell" is [A1], which does NOT take mu-/mi-. mosulti / misulti is the [A2] sense "speak,
#   utter", so the row says speak, not say.
# - kita in ma-/na- was REMOVED. makita / nakita is not an actor pair like matulog / natulog: Wolff
#   gives "Makita ba nimu ang ayruplanu? Can you see the plane?", where the one who sees is nimu
#   and the thing seen is the subject. That is object focus, which is deferred. Drilling it beside
#   matulog would teach "makita ko" for "I will see", which means "I will be seen".
# Every row must also be a pair native news uses (tests/test_ceb_affix_patterns.py enforces it).
